class Game(Scene):
    """The main game class."""

    # Set your game name/version here.
    NAME = 'Delta Time Demo'
    VERSION = '1.0'

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        options: dict[str, object],
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None = None,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the Game.

        Args:
            options (dict[str, object]): The options passed to the game.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()  # type: ignore[type-arg]

        super().__init__(options=options, groups=groups)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        # The bundled default font, loaded from its file through FontManager (cached): never a
        # system font scan (BUGS.md #156, #173 item 3: this asked for Calibri). It is a
        # pygame.font font: render() below takes (text, antialias, color).
        self.font = cast(
            'pygame.font.Font',
            FontManager.pygame_font(font_config={'font_name': DEFAULT_FONT_NAME, 'font_size': 40}),
        )
        self.rect_pos = 0
        # Pixels per second; use a visible speed
        self.velocity = 300
        self.record = 0
        self.passed = False
        self.start = False

    @classmethod
    def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
        """Add game-specific arguments to the gloal parser.

        This class method will get called automatically by the GameEngine class.

        Args:
            parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

        """
        parser.add_argument(
            '-v',
            '--version',
            action='store_true',
            help='print the game version and exit',
        )

        parser.add_argument(
            '-b',
            '--balls',
            type=int,
            help='the number of balls to start with',
            default=1,
        )

    @override
    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Update the scene.

        This method will get called automatically by the GameEngine class.

        Args:
            dt: The delta time (float).

        """
        if self.start:
            self.dt_timer += dt
            self.rect_pos += self.velocity * dt

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the scene.

        This method will get called automatically by the GameEngine class.

        """
        assert self.screen is not None
        self.screen.fill((0, 0, 0))

        if self.rect_pos > self.screen_width and not self.passed:
            self.record = self.dt_timer
            self.passed = True

        countdown = self.font.render(
            'Time: ' + str(round(self.dt_timer, 2)),
            False,  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]
            (255, 255, 255),
        )
        fps_text = self.font.render(f'FPS: {round(self.fps, 2)}', False, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

        self.screen.blit(countdown, (0, 0))
        self.screen.blit(fps_text, (0, 50))

        pygame.draw.rect(self.screen, WHITE, (self.rect_pos, (self.screen_height / 2) + 30, 40, 40))
        if self.record:
            record_text = self.font.render(f'Time: {round(self.record, 2)}', False, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

            self.screen.blit(record_text, (self.screen_width / 4, self.screen_height / 2))

    @override
    def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key down events.

        Args:
            event (KeyEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        if current_input().key_pressed(pygame.K_SPACE):
            self.start = True

debug_subject property #

The scene the debug overlay inspects: normally this scene itself.

A scene that only presents another scene (PauseScene shows a frozen screenshot of the paused game) returns that scene, so its hitboxes and physics stay visible and line up with the frozen picture.

game_time property #

Logic seconds since this scene started: the sum of the dt its dt_tick received.

Capped by MAX_FRAME_SECONDS where set, and it does not advance while the scene is not running (paused, or switched away), so cooldowns and timers measured with it pause with the game and replay exactly. Use it for gameplay timing instead of the wall clock.

input_devices property #

Every joystick and game controller the game sees, by instance id.

Each InputDevice reads the frame's input snapshot on its joystick layer and, for a mapped pad, its controller layer; its events reach on_*_event from one layer only (glitchygames/input/input_devices.py). Empty without an engine.

scene_start property #

How this scene began, once set up (glitchygames/scene_start.py).

None when its start was not captured (live play without recording, playback or instant replay) or before its first setup.

screenshot property #

A screenshot of the scene.

__subclasshook__(subclass) classmethod #

Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:
  • bool( bool ) –

    True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def advance_game_time(self: Self, *, seconds: float) -> None:
    """Add one frame's scene dt to game_time.

    The engine calls this once per scene frame (SceneManager._update_scene, before
    dt_tick); games read game_time and never call it. It is public only because the scene
    manager, another class, calls it.

    Args:
        seconds: The scene's (possibly capped) dt this frame.

    """
    self._game_time_seconds += seconds

camera_target() #

The world point the engine aims the camera at this frame, or None (manual camera).

Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus). The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

def camera_target(self: Self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """The world point the engine aims the camera at this frame, or None (manual camera).

    Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus).
    The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The
    engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

    Returns:
        tuple[float, float] | None: The target's (world_x, world_y), or None when the
            camera follows nothing.

    """
    target = self.camera.follow_target
    if target is None:
        return None
    # Camera2D.follow() checked that the target has world_x and world_y
    return (float(target.world_x), float(target.world_y))

forget_key_presses() #

Forget every key press recorded by record_key_press.

SceneManager calls this whenever the scene becomes active (switched to, resumed, or the target of a transition), before setup(). A press whose release went to another scene would otherwise stay recorded, and a later release of that key (whose press was discarded during a transition) would quit. Games never call it; it is public only because the scene manager calls it.

def forget_key_presses(self: Self) -> None:
    """Forget every key press recorded by record_key_press.

    SceneManager calls this whenever the scene becomes active (switched to, resumed, or
    the target of a transition), before setup(). A press whose release went to another
    scene would otherwise stay recorded, and a later release of that key (whose press was
    discarded during a transition) would quit.
    Games never call it; it is public only because the scene manager calls it.
    """
    self._keys_pressed_in_scene.clear()

def game_over(self: Self) -> None:
    """Handle game over for the current scene.

    Default implementation switches to a GameOverScene.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom game over behavior.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.game_over_scene import GameOverScene

    # Create the game over scene
    game_over_scene = GameOverScene(options=self.options)

    # Switch to the game over scene
    self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(game_over_scene)

    self.log.info('Game over')

@override
def on_fps_event(self: Self, event: events.FpsEvent) -> None:
    """Handle FPS events.

    Args:
        event (FpsEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    # FPSEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 1
    # Log FPS at the specified interval to reduce log spam. The frame clock starts at 0, so
    # the first log waits one full interval of play
    current_time = frame_clock_seconds()

    # Use the configured log interval instead of hardcoded 1.0 second
    log_interval_seconds = float(self.scene_manager.fps_log_interval_ms) / 1000.0
    if current_time - self._last_fps_log_time >= log_interval_seconds:
        event_fps: float = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)
        self.log.info('Scene "%s" (%s) FPS: %s', self.NAME, type(self), event_fps)
        self._last_fps_log_time = current_time

    self.fps = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)

@override
def on_key_up_event(self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> None:
    """Handle key up events.

    Args:
        event (KeyEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('%s: On Key Up Event %s', type(self), event)

    # Check for focused sprites first
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()

    # Only a release whose press this scene received can quit (record_key_press): a key
    # pressed during a transition (the press is discarded) or in a scene that has since
    # been left must not quit from here. Each release consumes its press.
    event_key: int | None = getattr(event, 'key', None)
    was_pressed_in_scene = event_key is not None and event_key in self._keys_pressed_in_scene
    if event_key is not None:  # pragma: no branch - a key release always has a key
        self._keys_pressed_in_scene.discard(event_key)

    # Only process quit keys if no sprites are focused
    if (
        not focused_sprites
        and was_pressed_in_scene
        and event_key in {pygame.K_q, pygame.K_ESCAPE}
    ):
        self._handle_quit_key_press()

@override
def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle left mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Left Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_left_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_left_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state
    if collided_sprites:
        top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
        self.log.debug(
            'Top sprite @ DOWN: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
            type(top_sprite).__name__,
            getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
            event_pos,
        )

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_mouse_drag_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseMotionEvent, trigger: object) -> None:
    """Handle mouse drag events.

    Args:
        event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.
        trigger (object): The event trigger.

    """
    self.log.debug('%s: Mouse Drag Event: %s %s', type(self), event, trigger)
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    # Optimized: Skip expensive collision detection for drag events
    # Most drag handling is done by specific sprite drag handlers
    # (e.g., on_left_mouse_drag_event)
    # Only do collision detection if specifically needed
    collided_sprites = self.sprites_at_position(pos=event_pos)

    # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state during drag
    if collided_sprites:
        top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
        self.log.debug(
            'Top sprite @ DRAG: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
            type(top_sprite).__name__,
            getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
            event_pos,
        )

    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        sprite.on_mouse_drag_event(event, trigger)

pause() #

Pause the current scene.

Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame. Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause() usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

@override
def pause(self: Self) -> None:
    """Pause the current scene.

    Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

    The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause()
    usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an
    immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.pause_scene import PauseScene

    self.next_scene = PauseScene(options=self.options)

    self.log.info('Scene pause requested')

record_key_press(*, key) #

Return the constructor arguments that rebuild this scene as it began (besides options).

A scene rebuilt for playback is type(scene)(**replay_arguments(), options=...) def resume(self: Self) -> None:
    """Resume the current scene.

    Default implementation switches back to the previous scene.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom resume behavior.

    """
    if self.scene_manager.previous_scene:
        self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(self.scene_manager.previous_scene)
        self.log.info('Scene resumed')
    else:
        self.log.warning('No previous scene found to resume')

def shake(self: Self, shake: Shake, *, targets: ShakeTarget = ShakeTarget.WORLD) -> None:
    """Start a shake on the world (camera), the whole screen, or both.

    Rumble, if the shake has it, is sent automatically by the scene manager.

    Args:
        shake: The shake to start.
        targets: ShakeTarget.WORLD, ShakeTarget.SCREEN, or both combined with |.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If WORLD is requested on a scene that is not active (for example
            from a transition cue, which runs after the scene was cleaned up).

    """
    if ShakeTarget.WORLD in targets:
        if self.scene_manager.active_scene is not self:
            message = f'{self.NAME} is not the active scene; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN'
            raise RuntimeError(message)
        self.camera.shake_effect.add(shake)
        if not self._world_shake_warning_logged and not self._world_shake_moves_anything():
            LOG.warning(
                'WORLD shake on %s has no effect: no sprites are positioned through its '
                'camera; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN',
                self.NAME,
            )
            self._world_shake_warning_logged = True
    if ShakeTarget.SCREEN in targets:
        self.scene_manager.screen_shake.add(shake)

@override
def update(self: Self) -> None:
    """Update the scene.

    This method will get called automatically by the GameEngine class.

    """
    assert self.screen is not None
    self.screen.fill((0, 0, 0))

    if self.rect_pos > self.screen_width and not self.passed:
        self.record = self.dt_timer
        self.passed = True

    countdown = self.font.render(
        'Time: ' + str(round(self.dt_timer, 2)),
        False,  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]
        (255, 255, 255),
    )
    fps_text = self.font.render(f'FPS: {round(self.fps, 2)}', False, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

    self.screen.blit(countdown, (0, 0))
    self.screen.blit(fps_text, (0, 50))

    pygame.draw.rect(self.screen, WHITE, (self.rect_pos, (self.screen_height / 2) + 30, 40, 40))
    if self.record:
        record_text = self.font.render(f'Time: {round(self.record, 2)}', False, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

        self.screen.blit(record_text, (self.screen_width / 4, self.screen_height / 2))

def main() -> None:

Joystick Demo: every connected joystick and game controller, live.

Run it with python -m glitchygames.examples.joystick_demo and plug devices in and out. Each device the engine sees (Scene.input_devices, glitchygames/input/input_devices.py) gets a column: its name, GUID, instance id and device index (the devices door's descriptor), the layer its events come from, then that layer's live axes, held buttons and hats. A mapped game pad shows its controller layer (CONTROLLER_AXIS_* / CONTROLLER_BUTTON_* ids, axes on pygame's int scale); any other device its joystick layer. The readout is drawn from the frame's input snapshot, so a replay of a recording shows exactly what the recorded run showed.

The header names the input mode (--input-mode: auto shows every device, joystick every device on its joystick layer, controller only mapped pads), the last device connected or disconnected, and the last input event and the handler it reached: each press arrives once, from the device's event layer.

Game #

class Game(Scene):
    """Shows every connected joystick and game controller with its live inputs."""

    NAME = 'Joystick Demo'
    VERSION = '1.0'

    def __init__(self: Self, options: dict[str, object]) -> None:
        """Create the demo with nothing reported yet.

        Args:
            options: The options passed to the game.

        """
        super().__init__(options=options)
        # A pygame.font font (FontManager caches it)
        self.font = cast(
            'pygame.font.Font',
            FontManager.pygame_font(
                font_config={'font_name': DEFAULT_FONT_NAME, 'font_size': FONT_SIZE}
            ),
        )
        self.last_device_change = NO_DEVICE_CHANGE
        self.last_input_event = NO_INPUT_EVENT

    def header_lines(self: Self) -> list[str]:
        """Return the header: the demo, the input mode, the device count and the last changes.

        Returns:
            The lines, top to bottom.

        """
        device_count = len(self.input_devices)
        return [
            f'{self.NAME} {self.VERSION}',
            f'Input mode: {self.input_devices.input_mode}',
            f'Devices: {device_count}' if device_count else 'No devices: plug one in',
            self.last_device_change,
            self.last_input_event,
        ]

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Draw the header, then one column per device, from this frame's input snapshot."""
        assert self.screen is not None
        self.screen.fill(BLACK)
        line_height = self.font.get_linesize() + LINE_SPACING
        header = self.header_lines()
        for line_number, line in enumerate(header):
            self._draw_line(
                text=line, color=WHITE, position=(MARGIN, MARGIN + line_number * line_height)
            )
        columns_top = MARGIN + (len(header) + 1) * line_height
        for column, device in enumerate(self.input_devices):
            column_left = MARGIN + column * COLUMN_WIDTH
            for line_number, line in enumerate(device_lines(device)):
                self._draw_line(
                    text=line,
                    color=YELLOW if line_number == 0 else WHITE,
                    position=(column_left, columns_top + line_number * line_height),
                )

    def _draw_line(
        self: Self, *, text: str, color: tuple[int, int, int], position: tuple[int, int]
    ) -> None:
        """Draw one line of the readout.

        Args:
            text: The line.
            color: Its colour.
            position: Its top-left corner on the screen.

        """
        assert self.screen is not None
        rendered = self.font.render(text, antialias=False, color=color)
        self.screen.blit(rendered, position)

    @override
    def on_input_device_added(self: Self, *, device: InputDevice) -> None:
        """Report a device that was plugged in (its column appears with the next frame).

        Args:
            device: The device.

        """
        self.last_device_change = f'Connected: {device.name}'
        LOG.info('Connected: %s (instance %d)', device.name, device.instance_id)

    @override
    def on_input_device_removed(self: Self, *, device: InputDevice) -> None:
        """Report a device that was unplugged (its column goes with the next frame).

        Args:
            device: The device.

        """
        self.last_device_change = f'Disconnected: {device.name}'
        LOG.info('Disconnected: %s (instance %d)', device.name, device.instance_id)

    def _report_input_event(self: Self, *, handler_name: str, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Show which handler an input event reached, from which device.

        Args:
            handler_name: The handler.
            event: The event (every joystick and controller input event has an instance id).

        """
        self.last_input_event = f'{handler_name} from instance {event.instance_id}'

    @override
    def on_joy_axis_motion_event(self: Self, event: JoyAxisEvent) -> None:
        """Report a joystick-layer axis motion.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_joy_axis_motion_event', event=event)

    @override
    def on_joy_ball_motion_event(self: Self, event: JoyBallEvent) -> None:
        """Report a joystick-layer trackball motion.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_joy_ball_motion_event', event=event)

    @override
    def on_joy_hat_motion_event(self: Self, event: JoyHatEvent) -> None:
        """Report a joystick-layer hat motion.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_joy_hat_motion_event', event=event)

    @override
    def on_joy_button_down_event(self: Self, event: JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Report a joystick-layer button press.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_joy_button_down_event', event=event)

    @override
    def on_joy_button_up_event(self: Self, event: JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Report a joystick-layer button release.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_joy_button_up_event', event=event)

    @override
    def on_controller_axis_motion_event(self: Self, event: ControllerAxisEvent) -> None:
        """Report a controller-layer axis motion.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_controller_axis_motion_event', event=event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_down_event(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Report a controller-layer button press.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_controller_button_down_event', event=event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_up_event(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Report a controller-layer button release.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        self._report_input_event(handler_name='on_controller_button_up_event', event=event)

    # Device lifecycle events: the engine tracks the devices and reports them through
    # on_input_device_added / on_input_device_removed, so these need nothing more

    @override
    def on_joy_device_added_event(self: Self, event: JoyDeviceAddedEvent) -> None:
        """Nothing to do: see on_input_device_added.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """

    @override
    def on_joy_device_removed_event(self: Self, event: JoyDeviceRemovedEvent) -> None:
        """Nothing to do: see on_input_device_removed.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """

    @override
    def on_controller_device_added_event(self: Self, event: ControllerDeviceAddedEvent) -> None:
        """Nothing to do: see on_input_device_added.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """

    @override
    def on_controller_device_removed_event(self: Self, event: ControllerDeviceEvent) -> None:
        """Nothing to do: see on_input_device_removed.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """

    @override
    def on_controller_device_remapped_event(self: Self, event: ControllerDeviceEvent) -> None:
        """Nothing to do: the readout follows the device's mapping every frame.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """

debug_subject property #

The scene the debug overlay inspects: normally this scene itself.

A scene that only presents another scene (PauseScene shows a frozen screenshot of the paused game) returns that scene, so its hitboxes and physics stay visible and line up with the frozen picture.

game_time property #

Logic seconds since this scene started: the sum of the dt its dt_tick received.

Capped by MAX_FRAME_SECONDS where set, and it does not advance while the scene is not running (paused, or switched away), so cooldowns and timers measured with it pause with the game and replay exactly. Use it for gameplay timing instead of the wall clock.

input_devices property #

Every joystick and game controller the game sees, by instance id.

Each InputDevice reads the frame's input snapshot on its joystick layer and, for a mapped pad, its controller layer; its events reach on_*_event from one layer only (glitchygames/input/input_devices.py). Empty without an engine.

scene_start property #

How this scene began, once set up (glitchygames/scene_start.py).

None when its start was not captured (live play without recording, playback or instant replay) or before its first setup.

screenshot property #

A screenshot of the scene.

__subclasshook__(subclass) classmethod #

Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:
  • bool( bool ) –

    True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def advance_game_time(self: Self, *, seconds: float) -> None:
    """Add one frame's scene dt to game_time.

    The engine calls this once per scene frame (SceneManager._update_scene, before
    dt_tick); games read game_time and never call it. It is public only because the scene
    manager, another class, calls it.

    Args:
        seconds: The scene's (possibly capped) dt this frame.

    """
    self._game_time_seconds += seconds

Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus). The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

def camera_target(self: Self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """The world point the engine aims the camera at this frame, or None (manual camera).

    Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus).
    The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The
    engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

    Returns:
        tuple[float, float] | None: The target's (world_x, world_y), or None when the
            camera follows nothing.

    """
    target = self.camera.follow_target
    if target is None:
        return None
    # Camera2D.follow() checked that the target has world_x and world_y
    return (float(target.world_x), float(target.world_y))

def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
    """Update the scene's delta time and active tweens.

    Args:
        dt (float): The delta time to update.

    """
    self.dt = dt
    self.dt_timer += self.dt
    self.tweens.update(dt)

forget_key_presses() #

Forget every key press recorded by record_key_press.

SceneManager calls this whenever the scene becomes active (switched to, resumed, or the target of a transition), before setup(). A press whose release went to another scene would otherwise stay recorded, and a later release of that key (whose press was discarded during a transition) would quit. Games never call it; it is public only because the scene manager calls it.

def forget_key_presses(self: Self) -> None:
    """Forget every key press recorded by record_key_press.

    SceneManager calls this whenever the scene becomes active (switched to, resumed, or
    the target of a transition), before setup(). A press whose release went to another
    scene would otherwise stay recorded, and a later release of that key (whose press was
    discarded during a transition) would quit.
    Games never call it; it is public only because the scene manager calls it.
    """
    self._keys_pressed_in_scene.clear()

def game_over(self: Self) -> None:
    """Handle game over for the current scene.

    Default implementation switches to a GameOverScene.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom game over behavior.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.game_over_scene import GameOverScene

    # Create the game over scene
    game_over_scene = GameOverScene(options=self.options)

    # Switch to the game over scene
    self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(game_over_scene)

    self.log.info('Game over')

@override
def on_fps_event(self: Self, event: events.FpsEvent) -> None:
    """Handle FPS events.

    Args:
        event (FpsEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    # FPSEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 1
    # Log FPS at the specified interval to reduce log spam. The frame clock starts at 0, so
    # the first log waits one full interval of play
    current_time = frame_clock_seconds()

    # Use the configured log interval instead of hardcoded 1.0 second
    log_interval_seconds = float(self.scene_manager.fps_log_interval_ms) / 1000.0
    if current_time - self._last_fps_log_time >= log_interval_seconds:
        event_fps: float = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)
        self.log.info('Scene "%s" (%s) FPS: %s', self.NAME, type(self), event_fps)
        self._last_fps_log_time = current_time

    self.fps = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)

@override
def on_key_up_event(self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> None:
    """Handle key up events.

    Args:
        event (KeyEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('%s: On Key Up Event %s', type(self), event)

    # Check for focused sprites first
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()

    # Only a release whose press this scene received can quit (record_key_press): a key
    # pressed during a transition (the press is discarded) or in a scene that has since
    # been left must not quit from here. Each release consumes its press.
    event_key: int | None = getattr(event, 'key', None)
    was_pressed_in_scene = event_key is not None and event_key in self._keys_pressed_in_scene
    if event_key is not None:  # pragma: no branch - a key release always has a key
        self._keys_pressed_in_scene.discard(event_key)

    # Only process quit keys if no sprites are focused
    if (
        not focused_sprites
        and was_pressed_in_scene
        and event_key in {pygame.K_q, pygame.K_ESCAPE}
    ):
        self._handle_quit_key_press()

@override
def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle left mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Left Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_left_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_left_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state
    if collided_sprites:
        top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
        self.log.debug(
            'Top sprite @ DOWN: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
            type(top_sprite).__name__,
            getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
            event_pos,
        )

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_mouse_drag_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseMotionEvent, trigger: object) -> None:
    """Handle mouse drag events.

    Args:
        event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.
        trigger (object): The event trigger.

    """
    self.log.debug('%s: Mouse Drag Event: %s %s', type(self), event, trigger)
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    # Optimized: Skip expensive collision detection for drag events
    # Most drag handling is done by specific sprite drag handlers
    # (e.g., on_left_mouse_drag_event)
    # Only do collision detection if specifically needed
    collided_sprites = self.sprites_at_position(pos=event_pos)

    # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state during drag
    if collided_sprites:
        top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
        self.log.debug(
            'Top sprite @ DRAG: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
            type(top_sprite).__name__,
            getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
            event_pos,
        )

    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        sprite.on_mouse_drag_event(event, trigger)

pause() #

Pause the current scene.

Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame. Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause() usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

@override
def pause(self: Self) -> None:
    """Pause the current scene.

    Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

    The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause()
    usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an
    immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.pause_scene import PauseScene

    self.next_scene = PauseScene(options=self.options)

    self.log.info('Scene pause requested')

record_key_press(*, key) #

Note that a key-down reached this scene.

SceneManager calls this for every key-down it routes to the active scene, before the scene's own on_key_down_event, so subclasses that override that handler are covered. on_key_up_event quits only on the release of a key recorded here. Return the constructor arguments that rebuild this scene as it began (besides options).

A scene rebuilt for playback is type(scene)(**replay_arguments(), options=...) def resume(self: Self) -> None:
    """Resume the current scene.

    Default implementation switches back to the previous scene.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom resume behavior.

    """
    if self.scene_manager.previous_scene:
        self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(self.scene_manager.previous_scene)
        self.log.info('Scene resumed')
    else:
        self.log.warning('No previous scene found to resume')

def shake(self: Self, shake: Shake, *, targets: ShakeTarget = ShakeTarget.WORLD) -> None:
    """Start a shake on the world (camera), the whole screen, or both.

    Rumble, if the shake has it, is sent automatically by the scene manager.

    Args:
        shake: The shake to start.
        targets: ShakeTarget.WORLD, ShakeTarget.SCREEN, or both combined with |.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If WORLD is requested on a scene that is not active (for example
            from a transition cue, which runs after the scene was cleaned up).

    """
    if ShakeTarget.WORLD in targets:
        if self.scene_manager.active_scene is not self:
            message = f'{self.NAME} is not the active scene; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN'
            raise RuntimeError(message)
        self.camera.shake_effect.add(shake)
        if not self._world_shake_warning_logged and not self._world_shake_moves_anything():
            LOG.warning(
                'WORLD shake on %s has no effect: no sprites are positioned through its '
                'camera; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN',
                self.NAME,
            )
            self._world_shake_warning_logged = True
    if ShakeTarget.SCREEN in targets:
        self.scene_manager.screen_shake.add(shake)

Draw the header, then one column per device, from this frame's input snapshot.

@override
def update(self: Self) -> None:
    """Draw the header, then one column per device, from this frame's input snapshot."""
    assert self.screen is not None
    self.screen.fill(BLACK)
    line_height = self.font.get_linesize() + LINE_SPACING
    header = self.header_lines()
    for line_number, line in enumerate(header):
        self._draw_line(
            text=line, color=WHITE, position=(MARGIN, MARGIN + line_number * line_height)
        )
    columns_top = MARGIN + (len(header) + 1) * line_height
    for column, device in enumerate(self.input_devices):
        column_left = MARGIN + column * COLUMN_WIDTH
        for line_number, line in enumerate(device_lines(device)):
            self._draw_line(
                text=line,
                color=YELLOW if line_number == 0 else WHITE,
                position=(column_left, columns_top + line_number * line_height),
            )

def device_lines(device: InputDevice) -> list[str]:
    """Return the readout of one device: who it is, then its event layer's positions now.

    Args:
        device: The device.

    Returns:
        The lines, top to bottom (the first, the device's name, is drawn highlighted).

    """
    descriptor = device.descriptor
    layer = device.event_layer
    held_buttons = [str(button) for button, held in enumerate(layer.buttons) if held]
    return [
        device.name,
        f'GUID: {descriptor.guid or "unknown"}',
        f'Instance {descriptor.instance_id}, device index {descriptor.device_index}',
        f'Events: {layer.kind} layer',
        *(f'Axis {axis}: {value}' for axis, value in enumerate(layer.axes)),
        f'Buttons held: {", ".join(held_buttons) or "none"}',
        *(f'Hat {hat}: {value}' for hat, value in enumerate(layer.hats)),
    ]

class Game(Scene):
    """The main game class."""

    log = LOG

    # Set your game name/version here.
    NAME = 'Input Demo'
    VERSION = '1.0'

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        options: dict[str, object],
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the Game.

        Args:
            options (dict[str, object]): The options passed to the game.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        super().__init__(options=options, groups=groups)
        self.input_box = InputBox(
            x=320,
            y=240,
            width=200,
            height=20,
            text='Test',
            groups=groups,
        )

        self.background_color = (255, 255, 0)

        self.all_sprites = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty(self.input_box)

        assert self.screen is not None
        self.all_sprites.clear(self.screen, self.background)

    @override
    def setup(self: Self) -> None:
        """Set up the game."""
        pygame.key.set_repeat(350)

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the game."""
        self.input_box.update()
        assert self.screen is not None
        assert self.input_box.image is not None
        self.screen.blit(self.input_box.image, (320, 240))

    def on_input_box_submit_event(self: Self, control: InputBox) -> None:
        """Handle input box submit events.

        Args:
            control: The control that submitted the event.

        """
        self.log.info('%s Got text input from: %s: %s', self.name, control.name, control.text)

    @override
    def on_mouse_button_up_event(self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse button up events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        self.input_box.activate()

    @override
    def on_key_up_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key up events.

        Args:
            event (KeyEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        if self.input_box.is_active:
            self.input_box.on_key_up_event(event)
        elif event.key == pygame.K_TAB:
            self.input_box.activate()
        else:
            super().on_key_up_event(event)

    @override
    def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key down events.

        Args:
            event (KeyEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        if self.input_box.is_active:
            # Return submits the text (the box itself has no parent to tell)
            if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN:
                self.on_input_box_submit_event(control=self.input_box)
            self.input_box.on_key_down_event(event)
        else:
            # Key down, not key up: a quit key quits on its release, not its press
            super().on_key_down_event(event)

debug_subject property #

The scene the debug overlay inspects: normally this scene itself.

A scene that only presents another scene (PauseScene shows a frozen screenshot of the paused game) returns that scene, so its hitboxes and physics stay visible and line up with the frozen picture.

game_time property #

Logic seconds since this scene started: the sum of the dt its dt_tick received.

Capped by MAX_FRAME_SECONDS where set, and it does not advance while the scene is not running (paused, or switched away), so cooldowns and timers measured with it pause with the game and replay exactly. Use it for gameplay timing instead of the wall clock.

input_devices property #

Every joystick and game controller the game sees, by instance id.

Each InputDevice reads the frame's input snapshot on its joystick layer and, for a mapped pad, its controller layer; its events reach on_*_event from one layer only (glitchygames/input/input_devices.py). Empty without an engine.

scene_start property #

How this scene began, once set up (glitchygames/scene_start.py).

None when its start was not captured (live play without recording, playback or instant replay) or before its first setup.

__subclasshook__(subclass) classmethod #

Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:
  • bool( bool ) –

    True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def camera_target(self: Self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """The world point the engine aims the camera at this frame, or None (manual camera).

    Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus).
    The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The
    engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

    Returns:
        tuple[float, float] | None: The target's (world_x, world_y), or None when the
            camera follows nothing.

    """
    target = self.camera.follow_target
    if target is None:
        return None
    # Camera2D.follow() checked that the target has world_x and world_y
    return (float(target.world_x), float(target.world_y))

def game_over(self: Self) -> None:
    """Handle game over for the current scene.

    Default implementation switches to a GameOverScene.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom game over behavior.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.game_over_scene import GameOverScene

    # Create the game over scene
    game_over_scene = GameOverScene(options=self.options)

    # Switch to the game over scene
    self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(game_over_scene)

    self.log.info('Game over')

@override
def on_fps_event(self: Self, event: events.FpsEvent) -> None:
    """Handle FPS events.

    Args:
        event (FpsEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    # FPSEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 1
    # Log FPS at the specified interval to reduce log spam. The frame clock starts at 0, so
    # the first log waits one full interval of play
    current_time = frame_clock_seconds()

    # Use the configured log interval instead of hardcoded 1.0 second
    log_interval_seconds = float(self.scene_manager.fps_log_interval_ms) / 1000.0
    if current_time - self._last_fps_log_time >= log_interval_seconds:
        event_fps: float = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)
        self.log.info('Scene "%s" (%s) FPS: %s', self.NAME, type(self), event_fps)
        self._last_fps_log_time = current_time

    self.fps = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)

@override
def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
    """Handle key down events.

    Args:
        event (KeyEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    if self.input_box.is_active:
        # Return submits the text (the box itself has no parent to tell)
        if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN:
            self.on_input_box_submit_event(control=self.input_box)
        self.input_box.on_key_down_event(event)
    else:
        # Key down, not key up: a quit key quits on its release, not its press
        super().on_key_down_event(event)

        self.input_box.activate()
    else:
        super().on_key_up_event(event)

@override
def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle left mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Left Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_left_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_left_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state
    if collided_sprites:
        top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
        self.log.debug(
            'Top sprite @ DOWN: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
            type(top_sprite).__name__,
            getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
            event_pos,
        )

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_mouse_drag_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseMotionEvent, trigger: object) -> None:
    """Handle mouse drag events.

    Args:
        event (MouseMotionEvent): The event to handle.
        trigger (object): The event trigger.

    """
    self.log.debug('%s: Mouse Drag Event: %s %s', type(self), event, trigger)
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    # Optimized: Skip expensive collision detection for drag events
    # Most drag handling is done by specific sprite drag handlers
    # (e.g., on_left_mouse_drag_event)
    # Only do collision detection if specifically needed
    collided_sprites = self.sprites_at_position(pos=event_pos)

    # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state during drag
    if collided_sprites:
        top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
        self.log.debug(
            'Top sprite @ DRAG: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
            type(top_sprite).__name__,
            getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
            event_pos,
        )

    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        sprite.on_mouse_drag_event(event, trigger)

pause() #

Pause the current scene.

Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame. Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause() usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

@override
def pause(self: Self) -> None:
    """Pause the current scene.

    Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

    The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause()
    usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an
    immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.pause_scene import PauseScene

    self.next_scene = PauseScene(options=self.options)

    self.log.info('Scene pause requested')

record_key_press(*, key) #

Note that a key-down reached this scene.

SceneManager calls this for every key-down it routes to the active scene, before the scene's own on_key_down_event, so subclasses that override that handler are covered. on_key_up_event quits only on the release of a key recorded here. Games never call it; it is public only because the scene manager, another class, calls it.

def record_key_press(self: Self, *, key: int) -> None:
    """Note that a key-down reached this scene.

    SceneManager calls this for every key-down it routes to the active scene, before the
    scene's own on_key_down_event, so subclasses that override that handler are covered.
    on_key_up_event quits only on the release of a key recorded here. Games never call it;
    it is public only because the scene manager, another class, calls it.

    Args:
        key: The pygame key code.

    """
    self._keys_pressed_in_scene.add(key)

def render(self: Self, screen: pygame.Surface) -> None:
    """Render the active scene.

    Args:
        screen (pygame.Surface): The screen to render to.

    # Use LayeredDirty's clear method for proper background clearing and dirty rect management
    self.all_sprites.clear(screen, self.background)
    self.rects = self.all_sprites.draw(screen)

replay_arguments() #

Return the constructor arguments that rebuild this scene as it began (besides options).

A scene rebuilt for playback is type(scene)(**replay_arguments(), options=...) (glitchygames/scene_start.py), so a scene built with arguments carried from the previous scene (a floor's score and lives) returns them as they were when it was built. They must read back from JSON exactly as returned. Asked once, before the scene's first setup, and only while its start is captured.

def resume(self: Self) -> None:
    """Resume the current scene.

    Default implementation switches back to the previous scene.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom resume behavior.

    """
    if self.scene_manager.previous_scene:
        self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(self.scene_manager.previous_scene)
        self.log.info('Scene resumed')
    else:
        self.log.warning('No previous scene found to resume')

def shake(self: Self, shake: Shake, *, targets: ShakeTarget = ShakeTarget.WORLD) -> None:
    """Start a shake on the world (camera), the whole screen, or both.

    Rumble, if the shake has it, is sent automatically by the scene manager.

    Args:
        shake: The shake to start.
        targets: ShakeTarget.WORLD, ShakeTarget.SCREEN, or both combined with |.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If WORLD is requested on a scene that is not active (for example
            from a transition cue, which runs after the scene was cleaned up).

    """
    if ShakeTarget.WORLD in targets:
        if self.scene_manager.active_scene is not self:
            message = f'{self.NAME} is not the active scene; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN'
            raise RuntimeError(message)
        self.camera.shake_effect.add(shake)
        if not self._world_shake_warning_logged and not self._world_shake_moves_anything():
            LOG.warning(
                'WORLD shake on %s has no effect: no sprites are positioned through its '
                'camera; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN',
                self.NAME,
            )
            self._world_shake_warning_logged = True
    if ShakeTarget.SCREEN in targets:
        self.scene_manager.screen_shake.add(shake)

def sprites_at_position(self: Self, pos: tuple[int, int]) -> list[Any]:
    """Return the sprites at a given position.

    Args:
        pos (tuple[int, int]): The position to check.

    Returns:
        list[Any]: The sprites at the given position.

    """
    mouse = MousePointer(pos=pos)

    return pygame.sprite.spritecollide(sprite=mouse, group=self.all_sprites, dokill=False)
